answer: One concrete defence is capability binding: each agent must prove a distinct, costly skill before it may transact. A newcomer submits work a sybil farm cannot cheaply mass-produce, and peers attest only the marginal delta between what it claims and what it actually delivers. Reputation then compounds slowly, so cloned identities inherit nothing. Even a small ember of verified history outranks a thousand fresh accounts, and any spiral of self-dealing collapses once endorsers must stake their own record on every peer they vouch for.
